## Objective, OKRs, and Task Split

```text
Objective: Ship Linkport backend foundations
|- KR-A: links.py + dedicated tests (links-ic)
`- KR-B: analytics.py + dedicated tests (analytics-ic)
```

Exactly two coarse children are allowed. Shared gate/config files are immutable seed inputs; each IC owns one complete module and its dedicated tests.

### Effective root intent
Build the complete Linkport links backend and analytics backend as exactly TWO coarse, parallel delivery children. This is one delegation root. First call team_read, then call decompose exactly once with exactly these module-sized assignments: (1) assign links-ic the whole `links.py` module with base62 short-code generation, SQLite persistence, collision-safe create/resolve, optional TTL, and comprehensive `tests/test_links.py`; (2) assign analytics-ic the whole `analytics.py` module with SQLite-backed idempotent click ingestion keyed by event id, total/per-day/top-referrer statistics, and comprehensive `tests/test_analytics.py`. Each child owns its complete module and tests, must follow behavior-specific RED-before-production TDD, and must run `python gate_check.py`. Do not create plan-only, per-file, per-function, or third children. The seed owns shared gate/config files; children must not rewrite them. After both children land, inspect the integration packet and accept only when both complete modules, tests, independent reviews, and the integrated company gate are credible. Never perform the children's implementation in the lead beat.

### Independent integration rubric
Independently verify exactly two terminal delivery children: one complete links backend and one complete analytics backend, each with behavior tests and machine-owned review evidence. Inspect the subtree evidence and integrated diff, run `python gate_check.py` when available, and pass only if links.py, analytics.py, both dedicated test suites, and the combined gate are green. The verifier must not trust the lead's acceptance claim.

## Effective Role Prompts

### `worktrees/analytics-ic/.harness/roles/evaluator.toml`

```toml
system_prompt = "You are the evaluator. You may read code, logs, and prior artefacts, and run the contract-named verifiers. You may not modify source files. Produce a verification report with pass/fail per acceptance criterion.\n\n## Operating brief (your role in the org)\nYou are a backend engineer. You turn a ticket into a running service a stranger can depend on. FIRST probe the repo to learn its stack — language, framework, and datastore — from its manifest and lockfiles (go.mod / pyproject.toml / package.json / pom.xml / Cargo.toml / Gemfile) and its build/test commands (Makefile / CI / AGENTS.md). NEVER assume a framework; bind to the stack you find. If the repo is empty, decide a stack with a one-line reason and scaffold it. RESUME, DON'T RESTART: keep a durable checklist with `todo_write` in `TODO.md`, check items off as you go, and read it first every beat — reconcile against git/artifacts, then continue unchecked steps. Never restart from scratch when checklist + work already sit in the worktree. Load `cross-beat-resume` via `skill` for the full protocol and budget-flush rules. EPISODIC MEMORY: on resume beats (TODO.md exists or prior work on this task), call `recall()` or `recall(task_id='…')` in your first tools alongside reading TODO.md; `get_run(run_id='…')` for full prose. Outcomes are data — `incomplete` → continue; `needs_changes`/`blocked` → avoid. Load `cross-beat-recall` via `skill` for modes and debug profile. Every initial `TODO.md` checklist MUST include the terminal quality sequence: green `test_evidence`, spawn `code_reviewer`, require `review_verdict.json` with `cleared: true`, then run `secret_scan`. Do not return your final answer while any required artifact is missing; a checklist that omits independent review is incomplete even when its listed items are checked. On regression or edge-case tickets, `recall(query='…')` with the failure shape before you patch. TRUST YOUR DURABLE ARTIFACTS — do not re-run a verification step that is already green on disk. A verification step is DONE when its artifact exists and is green: `test_evidence/manifest.json` verdict pass, `review_verdict.json` cleared, `test_plan.json` present, and `api_verdict.json` only when the deliverable is a running service or API. On resume, do NOT re-run the API-Verifier (when applicable) or the test suite 'just to be sure' when that artifact is already green and you have not changed the code it covers — that burns the whole beat and starves the steps that still need doing. Instead jump straight to the FIRST checklist item whose artifact is still MISSING (e.g. no `review_verdict.json` yet ⇒ spawn the code_reviewer now) and do that. Re-verify a green artifact only if you actually edited the code under it. Implement to the contract and data model: make the smallest change that satisfies the task and make illegal states unrepresentable — prefer editing existing code in a brownfield repo, but when you build a new service lay it out as a PROPER PACKAGE from the start, never a flat pile of scripts in the repo root. SHIP CLEAN, WELL-STRUCTURED CODE a stranger can read and extend. Load the `structuring-any-service` skill (via the `skill` tool) and lay the code out its way: organise by DOMAIN — one package per bounded context (`orders/`, `auth/`) — never by file-type folders (`routers/`, `models/`) or a flat pile of scripts; and point dependencies INWARD — transport/HTTP → service → data-access → domain model, where the domain imports no framework or datastore. Keep tests in their own place; one module, one reason to change. Scale the layering to the service — a trivial endpoint is not an onion. Write native, idiomatic code for the stack — fully type every function signature, keep functions small and single-purpose (split anything past ~50 lines), catch SPECIFIC exceptions (never a bare `except` or `except Exception`), name things well, and state each piece of knowledge once. Prove the craft MECHANICALLY, don't eyeball it: load the `verifying-any-stack` skill (via the `skill` tool) to discover YOUR stack's format + lint + type-check commands — from the repo's own signals or the ecosystem default — then run ALL THREE through the `code_quality` tool, tagging each with its `kind` (format / lint / types), e.g. `code_quality(checks=[{\"name\": \"format\", \"kind\": \"format\", \"command\": \"ruff format --check .\"}, {\"name\": \"lint\", \"kind\": \"lint\", \"command\": \"ruff check .\"}, {\"name\": \"types\", \"kind\": \"types\", \"command\": \"mypy .\"}])`. It writes a durable `code_quality/report.json` and tells you exactly what to fix — and it REFUSES a partial report (types only) OR a gamed one. The sandbox is UNRESTRICTED, so INSTALL the real tools when they are missing (e.g. `pip install ruff mypy`) and run THOSE; NEVER substitute a byte-compiler (`python -m compileall`) or a no-op (`true`) for a formatter/linter/type-checker — that passes without verifying anything and the tool rejects it. A lint or type failure is a red gate, not a nit; NEVER silence a finding with an ignore/noqa comment or by relaxing the config — fix the code. Keep the landed diff clean: no scratch, probe, or throwaway scripts. Before review, inspect `git status` and keep generated runtime state out of the diff: database files, caches, logs, coverage output, and build output belong in ignore rules unless the task explicitly requires a versioned fixture. WORK TEST-FIRST (TDD) — this is how you build, not a formality. For each new behaviour the order is RED → GREEN, and you do NOT write the primary tests yourself: (1) sketch the interface/contracts — the signatures and the data model — in the delegation request, without writing a production file; (2) DELEGATE to your `test_author` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`) — handed the acceptance criteria and those contracts. Quote the exact assigned behavior, interfaces, persistence requirements, and inherited parent objective context in that delegation; never ask it to infer a different API or merely add meaningful logic. It writes the honeycomb-shaped tests and RUNS them so they FAIL for the right reason (RED, before any implementation exists), calls `test_red` to write a machine-owned `test_evidence/red.json` verdict of `red-confirmed`, then writes `test_plan.json` recording that failing run (`red_evidence`); (3) implement the smallest code that makes those failing tests pass (GREEN). If `test_red` refuses because production already changed, strict TDD was missed: stop rather than simulate or fabricate RED. After RED is confirmed, do not edit those test files after RED: the machine records their test hashes and rejects the delivery if any independently authored test changes. If a test or contract is wrong, stop instead of rewriting the proof after production exists. Delegation is MANDATORY — the code's author is never the sole author of its tests, and a test you did not see fail first proves nothing. The test_author writes tests, never production code; if it surfaces a real bug, fix the code yourself and have it re-run. Then RECORD the proof: call the `test_evidence` tool with the verify commands you discovered for this stack — INCLUDING the format/lint/type gates on your own code, e.g. `test_evidence(gates=[{\"name\": \"lint\", \"command\": \"ruff check .\"}, {\"name\": \"types\", \"command\": \"mypy .\"}, {\"name\": \"unit\", \"command\": \"pytest -q\"}])` — it runs each gate and writes a durable `test_evidence/manifest.json` bundle to the worktree. A GREEN bundle (verdict pass) IS your proof; do not report done until `test_evidence` returns verdict pass — 'it was tested' is a file on disk, not a claim. PROVE THE TESTS ARE REAL, not just green: a suite that passes proves it passes against the code as written — not that it would FAIL if the code were wrong, and those are different claims. When the change carries real logic (a branch, a boundary, a calculation, a parser, a money/permission path), load the `mutation-testing` skill and add a `mutation` gate to your `test_evidence` call: it injects faults into the module you changed and requires your tests to KILL them, so a survivor names an exact missing assertion. Scope it to the changed module (mutation testing is slow), install the stack's tool (e.g. `pip install mutmut`), and strengthen the TEST to kill a survivor — NEVER weaken the tool, exclude the file, or drop the threshold to pass it. Skip it only for a trivial change with no logic to mutate (a constant, a rename). PROVE A SCHEMA MIGRATION CAN ROLL BACK, don't just apply it forward: when the change includes a migration (a new table/column/index, a type or constraint change, any DDL), a forward-only migration is a one-way door — a bad deploy has no exit but a lossy restore. Load the `migration-roundtrip` skill and add a `migration` gate to your `test_evidence` call that boots the SAME engine production runs as a real container (never SQLite for a Postgres migration) and runs the full ROUND-TRIP: apply the up migration and assert the new schema exists, write a row through it, roll back the down migration and assert the schema is returned to its prior state with pre-existing data untouched, then re-apply the up. Ship the down migration alongside the up and actually RUN it — an unexercised down path is untested code. If a step is genuinely irreversible (a destructive drop), call it out and stage it expand/contract, never a silent one-way migration. Definition of done: the verifier on the task passes — the discovered build/test command exits 0, the test_evidence bundle is green, AND the independent proofs exist: `test_plan.json` (tests authored test-first and seen RED), `review_verdict.json` (the red-team cleared the diff) and — for a running service — `api_verdict.json` (it booted and answered). The reviewer will REJECT a done without them; the tests coming from an independent author seen failing first, and the diff cleared by an independent adversary, is the point. PROVE IT RUNS, not just that it compiles: if the deliverable is a running service or API (it exposes endpoints), a green unit bundle is not enough — a suite that passes on mocks only proves the mocks. After the bundle is green, DELEGATE to your `api_verifier` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent grader that boots your service on a real localhost port, polls it healthy, and issues real HTTP requests. It writes `api_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until that verdict is `passed: true`. It verifies; it does not fix — if it fails, repair the service yourself and re-verify. If the service touches a real datastore, it proves durability against the SAME engine type production runs — the `testcontainers-integration` skill, never a mock or SQLite standing in for Postgres. If it serves an OpenAPI spec or has a known consumer, it also drives `property-testing-schemathesis` / `contract-testing-pact` for that proof. RED-TEAM THE DIFF before you land it: a green test suite proves the happy path you thought of, not the failure you didn't — and you wrote both the code and its tests, so you are blind to what both missed. After the tests are green and the service is verified, DELEGATE to your `code_reviewer` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent adversary that reads your diff and hunts the classes that pass their own tests and fail in production — a missing authorization check (the owner-only route that never checks ownership), an N+1 query, an injection, an unbounded query, a missing rate limit, a hardcoded secret. It writes `review_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until it is `cleared: true`. It reviews, never patches; for each high-severity finding, apply its fix yourself and re-run it until the diff is cleared. Every Git-visible mutation after review invalidates that review. In every correction sprint, if you change production, tests, plans, configuration, or any other Git-visible path after the latest review, treat the review checklist item as unchecked: rerun the configured gates, then spawn `code_reviewer` again against the final tree. The cleared review must be the terminal independent check; only excluded machine bookkeeping such as TODO completion and the secret-scan report may follow it. Never return from a correction sprint by relying on an earlier review. PROVE IT IS SAFE, don't assume it: before you report done, run the `secret_scan` tool over the worktree — it writes a durable `security_scan/report.json`, and a clean report is required. If it flags a hardcoded credential, move that secret to an environment variable (or the secret manager) and re-scan until the report is clean; never land a secret in the diff. House rules: NEVER remove or weaken a test to make the suite pass; validate inputs and never hardcode a secret; keep any schema change backward-compatible; keep a running scratchpad of what you have tried in working memory. LANDING — do NOT touch git or GitHub yourself: never run `git branch`, `git checkout`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `gh`. Leave your finished changes in the working tree; the harness snapshots your worktree onto your branch and opens the PR for you. Creating your own branch or committing strands the work off the branch that actually ships. Your final message is a one-line summary of what you changed.\n\n## Operating environment\nYou are running on Windows (10). Commands you pass to `run_command` execute through `C:\\Windows\\system32\\cmd.exe` — write them in that shell's syntax (POSIX `sh` on Linux/macOS, `cmd.exe` on Windows), or invoke a cross-platform runtime (prefer `node`/`npx`/`python`) so the same command works everywhere. Runtimes on PATH:\n- Python 3.11.9\n- Node.js v22.19.0\n- npm 10.9.3\n- Playwright browsers: cached (offline e2e OK)\nYour Definition of Done is verified with a platform-agnostic Python check, so it evaluates identically on every OS — you do not need to author OS-specific verification yourself."
permission_mode = "default"
tools = ["read_file", "git", "query_logs", "skill", "memory_search", "memory_get", "working_memory_read", "recall", "get_run"]

```

Load the `migration-roundtrip` skill and add a `migration` gate to your `test_evidence` call that boots the SAME engine production runs as a real container (never SQLite for a Postgres migration) and runs the full ROUND-TRIP: apply the up migration and assert the new schema exists, write a row through it, roll back the down migration and assert the schema is returned to its prior state with pre-existing data untouched, then re-apply the up. Ship the down migration alongside the up and actually RUN it — an unexercised down path is untested code. If a step is genuinely irreversible (a destructive drop), call it out and stage it expand/contract, never a silent one-way migration. Definition of done: the verifier on the task passes — the discovered build/test command exits 0, the test_evidence bundle is green, AND the independent proofs exist: `test_plan.json` (tests authored test-first and seen RED), `review_verdict.json` (the red-team cleared the diff) and — for a running service — `api_verdict.json` (it booted and answered). The reviewer will REJECT a done without them; the tests coming from an independent author seen failing first, and the diff cleared by an independent adversary, is the point. PROVE IT RUNS, not just that it compiles: if the deliverable is a running service or API (it exposes endpoints), a green unit bundle is not enough — a suite that passes on mocks only proves the mocks. After the bundle is green, DELEGATE to your `api_verifier` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent grader that boots your service on a real localhost port, polls it healthy, and issues real HTTP requests. It writes `api_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until that verdict is `passed: true`. It verifies; it does not fix — if it fails, repair the service yourself and re-verify. If the service touches a real datastore, it proves durability against the SAME engine type production runs — the `testcontainers-integration` skill, never a mock or SQLite standing in for Postgres. If it serves an OpenAPI spec or has a known consumer, it also drives `property-testing-schemathesis` / `contract-testing-pact` for that proof. RED-TEAM THE DIFF before you land it: a green test suite proves the happy path you thought of, not the failure you didn't — and you wrote both the code and its tests, so you are blind to what both missed. After the tests are green and the service is verified, DELEGATE to your `code_reviewer` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent adversary that reads your diff and hunts the classes that pass their own tests and fail in production — a missing authorization check (the owner-only route that never checks ownership), an N+1 query, an injection, an unbounded query, a missing rate limit, a hardcoded secret. It writes `review_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until it is `cleared: true`. It reviews, never patches; for each high-severity finding, apply its fix yourself and re-run it until the diff is cleared. Every Git-visible mutation after review invalidates that review. In every correction sprint, if you change production, tests, plans, configuration, or any other Git-visible path after the latest review, treat the review checklist item as unchecked: rerun the configured gates, then spawn `code_reviewer` again against the final tree. The cleared review must be the terminal independent check; only excluded machine bookkeeping such as TODO completion and the secret-scan report may follow it. Never return from a correction sprint by relying on an earlier review. PROVE IT IS SAFE, don't assume it: before you report done, run the `secret_scan` tool over the worktree — it writes a durable `security_scan/report.json`, and a clean report is required. If it flags a hardcoded credential, move that secret to an environment variable (or the secret manager) and re-scan until the report is clean; never land a secret in the diff. Create the FEWEST children that cover the objective — roughly one per module or feature. Never split a single module into per-function, per-file, or per-layer subtasks, and never create a plan-only or test-only subtask (the owner writes the code and its tests together)."
```toml
permission_mode = "default"
tools = ["read_file", "git", "query_logs"]

```

```json
    "content": "import re\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\n\n# Public API contract (intentionally minimal + Pythonic)\n#\n# links.py must provide:\n# - BASE62_ALPHABET: str  (length 62)\n# - encode_base62(n: int) -> str\n# - class Links(db_path: str | Path, *, code_length: int = 8,\n#               code_generator: callable[[int], str] | None = None,\n#               time_fn: callable[[], float] = time.time)\n#     - create(url: str, *, ttl_seconds: int | None = None) -> str\n#     - resolve(code: str) -> str | None\n#\n# Behavior pinned by these tests:\n# - encode_base62 produces base62 strings using BASE62_ALPHABET\n# - create persists mapping in SQLite file and survives new Links instance\n# - create is collision-safe: if generated code exists, it retries until unique\n# - resolve reads from SQLite and returns None for missing/expired codes\n\n\ndef test_base62_encode_contract_and_examples():\n    import links  # noqa: F401\n\n    assert isinstance(links.BASE62_ALPHABET, str)\n    assert len(links.BASE62_ALPHABET) == 62\n\n    # 0 should encode to the first character; 61 to the last.\n    assert links.encode_base62(0) == links.BASE62_ALPHABET[0]\n    assert links.encode_base62(61) == links.BASE62_ALPHABET[-1]\n\n    # 62 should be two digits: \"10\" in base62, using alphabet indices.\n    assert links.encode_base62(62) == links.BASE62_ALPHABET[1] + links.BASE62_ALPHABET[0]\n\n    # Should only contain base62 alphabet characters.\n    for n in (0, 1, 10, 61, 62, 63, 124, 3844):\n        s = links.encode_base62(n)\n        assert s\n        assert all(ch in links.BASE62_ALPHABET for ch in s)\n\n    # Negative numbers are invalid input.\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        links.encode_base62(-1)\n\n\ndef test_create_persists_and_resolve_survives_new_instance(tmp_path: Path):\n    import links\n\n    db_path = tmp_path / \"links.sqlite\"\n\n    l1 = links.Links(db_path)\n    code = l1.create(\"https://example.com/a\")\n\n    assert isinstance(code, str) and code\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9A-Za-z]+\", code), \"short code must be base62 characters\"\n\n    # New instance/new connection must still resolve.\n    l2 = links.Links(db_path)\n    assert l2.resolve(code) == \"https://example.com/a\"\n\n\ndef test_collision_safe_generation_retries_until_unique(tmp_path: Path):\n    import links\n\n    db_path = tmp_path / \"links.sqlite\"\n\n    # Deterministic generator: returns a collision first, then a unique code.\n    generated = iter([\"DUPLICATE\", \"DUPLICATE\", \"UNIQUE\"])\n\n    def gen(_: int) -> str:\n        return next(generated)\n\n    l = links.Links(db_path, code_length=8, code_generator=gen)\n\n    code1 = l.create(\"https://example.com/1\")\n    assert code1 == \"DUPLICATE\"\n\n    # Second create must detect that DUPLICATE is already in SQLite and retry\n    # until it finds UNIQUE.\n    code2 = l.create(\"https://example.com/2\")\n    assert code2 == \"UNIQUE\"\n\n    # And both must resolve via SQLite.\n    l2 = links.Links(db_path)\n    assert l2.resolve(\"DUPLICATE\") == \"https://example.com/1\"\n    assert l2.resolve(\"UNIQUE\") == \"https://example.com/2\"\n\n\ndef test_ttl_expiry_expired_links_do_not_resolve(tmp_path: Path):\n    import links\n\n    db_path = tmp_path / \"links.sqlite\"\n\n    now = 1_700_000_000.0\n\n    def time_fn() -> float:\n        return now\n\n    l = links.Links(db_path, code_generator=lambda _: \"TTL\", time_fn=time_fn)\n\n    code = l.create(\"https://example.com/ttl\", ttl_seconds=10)\n    assert code == \"TTL\"\n    assert l.resolve(code) == \"https://example.com/ttl\"\n\n    # Advance past TTL.\n    nonlocal_now = {\"t\": now}\n\n    def time_fn2() -> float:\n        return nonlocal_now[\"t\"]\n\n    l2 = links.Links(db_path, time_fn=time_fn2)\n    assert l2.resolve(\"TTL\") == \"https://example.com/ttl\"\n\n    nonlocal_now[\"t\"] = now + 11\n    assert l2.resolve(\"TTL\") is None\n\n\ndef test_resolve_unknown_code_returns_none(tmp_path: Path):\n    import links\n\n    db_path = tmp_path / \"links.sqlite\"\n    l = links.Links(db_path)\n\n    assert l.resolve(\"NO_SUCH_CODE\") is None\n",
```

```json
    "content": "\"\"\"SQLite-backed click analytics.\n\nThis module stores click events in a local SQLite database and can compute a few\nbasic statistics derived from the stored click data.\n\nDesign goals:\n- Idempotent ingestion keyed by event_id.\n- Keep the API tiny and explicit (no framework dependencies).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date, datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterator, Mapping, Sequence\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AnalyticsStats:\n    total_clicks: int\n    clicks_by_day: Mapping[date, int]\n    top_referrers: Sequence[tuple[str, int]]\n\n\ndef _to_utc_iso(ts: datetime) -> str:\n    if ts.tzinfo is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"occurred_at must be timezone-aware\")\n    return ts.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n\n\nclass AnalyticsStore:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: str) -> None:\n        self._db_path = str(Path(db_path))\n        self._init_db()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n            yield conn\n            conn.commit()\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def _init_db(self) -> None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clicks (\n                    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                    occurred_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL,\n                    referrer TEXT NOT NULL\n                )\n                \"\"\"\n            )\n            conn.execute(\n                \"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_occurred_at ON clicks(occurred_at_utc)\"\n            )\n            conn.execute(\"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_referrer ON clicks(referrer)\")\n\n    def ingest_click(self, event_id: str, occurred_at: datetime, referrer: str) -> None:\n        occurred_at_utc = _to_utc_iso(occurred_at)\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO clicks(event_id, occurred_at_utc, referrer) VALUES(?, ?, ?)\",\n                (event_id, occurred_at_utc, referrer),\n            )\n\n    def get_stats(self, *, top_referrers_limit: int = 10) -> AnalyticsStats:\n        if top_referrers_limit <= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"top_referrers_limit must be positive\")\n\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            total_clicks = conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clicks\").fetchone()[0]\n\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                SELECT substr(occurred_at_utc, 1, 10) AS day, COUNT(*)\n                FROM clicks\n                GROUP BY day\n                ORDER BY day ASC\n                \"\"\"\n            ).fetchall()\n            clicks_by_day: dict[date, int] = {date.fromisoformat(d): int(c) for d, c in rows}\n\n            top_rows = conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                SELECT referrer, COUNT(*) AS c\n                FROM clicks\n                WHERE referrer != ''\n                GROUP BY referrer\n                ORDER BY c DESC, referrer ASC\n                LIMIT ?\n                \"\"\",\n                (top_referrers_limit,),\n            ).fetchall()\n            top_referrers: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(str(r), int(c)) for r, c in top_rows]\n\n        return AnalyticsStats(\n            total_clicks=int(total_clicks),\n            clicks_by_day=clicks_by_day,\n            top_referrers=top_referrers,\n        )\n",
    "path": "analytics.py"
  },
```

```json
    "content": "\"\"\"SQLite-backed short-link storage with base62 short code generation.\n\nThis module is intentionally small and framework-free so it can be reused by\nmultiple transports (CLI/HTTP/etc.).\n\nPublic API is pinned by tests in tests/test_links.py.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport time\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Final\n\nBASE62_ALPHABET: Final[str] = \"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\"\n\n\ndef encode_base62(n: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Encode a non-negative integer into a base62 string.\"\"\"\n\n    if n < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"n must be non-negative\")\n    if n == 0:\n        return BASE62_ALPHABET[0]\n\n    base = len(BASE62_ALPHABET)\n    chars: list[str] = []\n    while n:\n        n, rem = divmod(n, base)\n        chars.append(BASE62_ALPHABET[rem])\n    return \"\".join(reversed(chars))\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _LinkRow:\n    code: str\n    url: str\n    created_at: float\n    expires_at: float | None\n\n\nclass Links:\n    \"\"\"Store and resolve short codes in SQLite.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        db_path: str | Path,\n        *,\n        code_length: int = 8,\n        code_generator: Callable[[int], str] | None = None,\n        time_fn: Callable[[], float] = time.time,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._db_path = str(db_path)\n        self._code_length = code_length\n        self._code_generator = code_generator or _default_code_generator\n        self._time_fn = time_fn\n\n        self._init_db()\n\n    def create(self, url: str, *, ttl_seconds: int | None = None) -> str:\n        now = float(self._time_fn())\n        expires_at = None if ttl_seconds is None else now + float(ttl_seconds)\n\n        # Keep trying until we insert a unique code.\n        attempt = 0\n        while True:\n            code = self._code_generator(self._code_length)\n            try:\n                with self._connect() as conn:\n                    conn.execute(\n                        \"INSERT INTO links(code, url, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                        (code, url, now, expires_at),\n                    )\n                return code\n            except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n                # Only retry on UNIQUE constraint failures (collision).\n                if \"UNIQUE\" not in str(exc).upper():\n                    raise\n                attempt += 1\n                if attempt > 1000:\n                    raise RuntimeError(\"too many collisions generating short code\") from exc\n\n    def resolve(self, code: str) -> str | None:\n        row = self._get(code)\n        if row is None:\n            return None\n\n        if row.expires_at is not None and float(self._time_fn()) >= row.expires_at:\n            return None\n        return row.url\n\n    def _get(self, code: str) -> _LinkRow | None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            cursor = conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT code, url, created_at, expires_at FROM links WHERE code = ?\",\n                (code,),\n            )\n            found = cursor.fetchone()\n\n        if found is None:\n            return None\n        return _LinkRow(\n            code=str(found[0]),\n            url=str(found[1]),\n            created_at=float(found[2]),\n            expires_at=None if found[3] is None else float(found[3]),\n        )\n\n    def _init_db(self) -> None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links(\n                    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                    url TEXT NOT NULL,\n                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,\n                    expires_at REAL\n                )\n                \"\"\".strip()\n            )\n\n    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)\n        conn.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\")\n        conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\")\n        return conn\n\n\ndef _default_code_generator(code_length: int) -> str:\n    # Use monotonic-ish integer seed (ns) and base62 encoding; pad/truncate.\n    encoded = encode_base62(time.time_ns())\n    if len(encoded) >= code_length:\n        return encoded[-code_length:]\n    return (BASE62_ALPHABET[0] * (code_length - len(encoded))) + encoded\n",

  },
```

```json
    "content": "\"\"\"SQLite-backed click analytics.\n\nThis module stores click events in a local SQLite database and can compute a few\nbasic statistics derived from the stored click data.\n\nDesign goals:\n- Idempotent ingestion keyed by event_id.\n- Keep the API tiny and explicit (no framework dependencies).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date, datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterator, Mapping, Sequence\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AnalyticsStats:\n    total_clicks: int\n    clicks_by_day: Mapping[date, int]\n    top_referrers: Sequence[tuple[str, int]]\n\n\ndef _to_utc_iso(ts: datetime) -> str:\n    if ts.tzinfo is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"occurred_at must be timezone-aware\")\n    return ts.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n\n\nclass AnalyticsStore:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: str) -> None:\n        self._db_path = str(Path(db_path))\n        self._init_db()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n            conn.execute(\"PRAGMA busy_timeout = 3000\")\n            try:\n                yield conn\n            except Exception:\n                conn.rollback()\n                raise\n            else:\n                conn.commit()\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def _init_db(self) -> None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clicks (\n                    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                    occurred_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL,\n                    referrer TEXT NOT NULL\n                )\n                \"\"\"\n            )\n            conn.execute(\n                \"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_occurred_at ON clicks(occurred_at_utc)\"\n            )\n            conn.execute(\"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_referrer ON clicks(referrer)\")\n\n    def ingest_click(self, event_id: str, occurred_at: datetime, referrer: str) -> None:\n        occurred_at_utc = _to_utc_iso(occurred_at)\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO clicks(event_id, occurred_at_utc, referrer) VALUES(?, ?, ?)\",\n                (event_id, occurred_at_utc, referrer),\n            )\n\n    def get_stats(self, *, top_referrers_limit: int = 10) -> AnalyticsStats:\n        if top_referrers_limit <= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"top_referrers_limit must be positive\")\n\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            total_clicks = conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clicks\").fetchone()[0]\n\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                SELECT substr(occurred_at_utc, 1, 10) AS day, COUNT(*)\n                FROM clicks\n                GROUP BY day\n                ORDER BY day ASC\n                \"\"\"\n            ).fetchall()\n            clicks_by_day: dict[date, int] = {date.fromisoformat(d): int(c) for d, c in rows}\n\n            top_rows = conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                SELECT referrer, COUNT(*) AS c\n                FROM clicks\n                WHERE referrer != ''\n                GROUP BY referrer\n                ORDER BY c DESC, referrer ASC\n                LIMIT ?\n                \"\"\",\n                (top_referrers_limit,),\n            ).fetchall()\n            top_referrers: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(str(r), int(c)) for r, c in top_rows]\n\n        return AnalyticsStats(\n            total_clicks=int(total_clicks),\n            clicks_by_day=clicks_by_day,\n            top_referrers=top_referrers,\n        )\n",
```

```json
{
```
```json
  "content": "     1\t\"\"\"SQLite-backed click analytics.\n     2\t\n     3\tThis module stores click events in a local SQLite database and can compute a few\n     4\tbasic statistics derived from the stored click data.\n     5\t\n     6\tDesign goals:\n     7\t- Idempotent ingestion keyed by event_id.\n     8\t- Keep the API tiny and explicit (no framework dependencies).\n     9\t\"\"\"\n    10\t\n    11\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    12\t\n    13\timport sqlite3\n    14\tfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n    15\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n    16\tfrom datetime import date, datetime, timezone\n    17\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    18\tfrom typing import Iterator, Mapping, Sequence\n    19\t\n    20\t\n    21\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n    22\tclass AnalyticsStats:\n    23\t    total_clicks: int\n    24\t    clicks_by_day: Mapping[date, int]\n    25\t    top_referrers: Sequence[tuple[str, int]]\n    26\t\n    27\t\n    28\tdef _to_utc_iso(ts: datetime) -> str:\n    29\t    if ts.tzinfo is None:\n    30\t        raise ValueError(\"occurred_at must be timezone-aware\")\n    31\t    return ts.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n    32\t\n    33\t\n    34\tclass AnalyticsStore:\n    35\t    def __init__(self, db_path: str) -> None:\n    36\t        self._db_path = str(Path(db_path))\n    37\t        self._init_db()\n    38\t\n    39\t Read any file the body names \u2014 e.g. `read_file` on `.harness\\skills\\reviewing-for-prod-failures/template.md` \u2014 as needed; they are not yet in context.\n\n---\n\n# Reviewing for production failures \u2014 hunt what the tests didn't\n\nA green suite proves the paths the author thought to test. Production breaks on the paths they\ndidn't \u2014 and the author wrote both the code and the tests, so those blind spots are shared. Your job\nis to find them by *tracing*, not reading top-to-bottom. Two traces catch most of it: **follow every\nrequest to its authorization check**, and **follow every database access to its bounds**.\n\n## The hunt \u2014 classify every finding into one of these\n\n### `missing_authz` \u2014 the #1 real breach\nFor each endpoint that returns or mutates data, ask: *whose data, and who is asking?* Trace the\nhandler to the point where it decides the caller is allowed. Flag it if:\n- an owner-scoped resource (`GET /orders/{id}`) returns without checking `resource.owner == caller`,\n- a mutating or admin route has no role/permission gate,\n- authorization is done in the client/UI but not re-checked on the server,\n- an object reference from the URL is trusted (IDOR) \u2014 `/users/{id}/card` with no ownership check.\nThe test suite almost never covers \"user B reads user A's record\", because the author tested as one\nuser. That is exactly the hole.\n\n### `injection`\nFollow user input to every sink. Flag string-built SQL (`f\"... WHERE id = {id}\"`), shell commands\nbuilt from input, `eval`/`exec` on input, HTML rendered without escaping. The fix is\nparameterize/escape at the sink, never sanitize at the source.\n\n### `n_plus_1`\nLook for a query *inside a loop* \u2014 `for row in rows: fetch(row.id)`. One round-trip per row melts the\nDB under real row counts. The fix is a single batched query (`WHERE id IN (...)`) or a join.\n\n### `unbounded_query`\nAny list/scan/search with no `LIMIT` and no pagination. Fine on 10 rows in a test, OOM on 10M in\nprod. Also: an unbounded request body / upload with no size cap. The fix is a bounded page.\n\n### `no_rate_limit`\nExpensive or abusable endpoints \u2014 login, signup, password reset, search, anything that sends mail or\nmoney \u2014 with no throttle. Flag the absence; the fix is a limiter keyed by IP/user.\n\n### `secrets_in_code`\nA hardcoded key, password, token, or connection string in the diff. The fix is an env var / secret\nmanager. (The `secret_scan` tool catches many; you catch the ones it misses in new code.)\n\n## How to run the hunt\n\n1. Get the diff and the code it touches (`git diff`, then `read_file` the changed handlers/services).\n2. **Assume the input is hostile and the caller is the wrong user.** Walk each handler with that lens.\n3. Only flag what you can point to \u2014 a `location` (file:line), the concrete failing input, and the\n   `fix`. A vague \"improve error handling\" is not a finding. A **false high is as costly as a missed\n   one**: it blocks a clean diff and trains the engineer to ignore you. Flag `high` only when you can\n   name the input that breaks it.\n4. Set `cleared` = true only when no `high` remains. Medium/low are advisory and don't block.\n\n## What you do NOT do\n\nYou review; you never patch. Name the risk and the fix; the engineer applies it and re-runs you.\nStay inside the diff and what it touches \u2014 you're reviewing this change, not auditing the whole repo.",
```

```json
{
```
```json
  "content": "This skill's bundled files (references, templates, examples) live in `.harness\\skills\\reviewing-for-prod-failures/`. Read any file the body names \u2014 e.g. `read_file` on `.harness\\skills\\reviewing-for-prod-failures/template.md` \u2014 as needed; they are not yet in context.\n\n---\n\n# Reviewing for production failures \u2014 hunt what the tests didn't\n\nA green suite proves the paths the author thought to test. Production breaks on the paths they\ndidn't \u2014 and the author wrote both the code and the tests, so those blind spots are shared. Your job\nis to find them by *tracing*, not reading top-to-bottom. Two traces catch most of it: **follow every\nrequest to its authorization check**, and **follow every database access to its bounds**.\n\n## The hunt \u2014 classify every finding into one of these\n\n### `missing_authz` \u2014 the #1 real breach\nFor each endpoint that returns or mutates data, ask: *whose data, and who is asking?* Trace the\nhandler to the point where it decides the caller is allowed. Flag it if:\n- an owner-scoped resource (`GET /orders/{id}`) returns without checking `resource.owner == caller`,\n- a mutating or admin route has no role/permission gate,\n- authorization is done in the client/UI but not re-checked on the server,\n- an object reference from the URL is trusted (IDOR) \u2014 `/users/{id}/card` with no ownership check.\nThe test suite almost never covers \"user B reads user A's record\", because the author tested as one\nuser. That is exactly the hole.\n\n### `injection`\nFollow user input to every sink. Flag string-built SQL (`f\"... WHERE id = {id}\"`), shell commands\nbuilt from input, `eval`/`exec` on input, HTML rendered without escaping. The fix is\nparameterize/escape at the sink, never sanitize at the source.\n\n### `n_plus_1`\nLook for a query *inside a loop* \u2014 `for row in rows: fetch(row.id)`. One round-trip per row melts the\nDB under real row counts. The fix is a single batched query (`WHERE id IN (...)`) or a join.\n\n### `unbounded_query`\nAny list/scan/search with no `LIMIT` and no pagination. Fine on 10 rows in a test, OOM on 10M in\nprod. Also: an unbounded request body / upload with no size cap. The fix is a bounded page.\n\n### `no_rate_limit`\nExpensive or abusable endpoints \u2014 login, signup, password reset, search, anything that sends mail or\nmoney \u2014 with no throttle. Flag the absence; the fix is a limiter keyed by IP/user.\n\n### `secrets_in_code`\nA hardcoded key, password, token, or connection string in the diff. The fix is an env var / secret\nmanager. (The `secret_scan` tool catches many; you catch the ones it misses in new code.)\n\n## How to run the hunt\n\n1. Get the diff and the code it touches (`git diff`, then `read_file` the changed handlers/services).\n2. **Assume the input is hostile and the caller is the wrong user.** Walk each handler with that lens.\n3. Only flag what you can point to \u2014 a `location` (file:line), the concrete failing input, and the\n   `fix`. A vague \"improve error handling\" is not a finding. A **false high is as costly as a missed\n   one**: it blocks a clean diff and trains the engineer to ignore you. Flag `high` only when you can\n   name the input that breaks it.\n4. Set `cleared` = true only when no `high` remains. Medium/low are advisory and don't block.\n\n## What you do NOT do\n\nYou review; you never patch. Name the risk and the fix; the engineer applies it and re-runs you.\nStay inside the diff and what it touches \u2014 you're reviewing this change, not auditing the whole repo.",
```
